# 長美債殖利率守在高檔，借款人加價換取資金

## 通膨放慢，仍未帶動長債反彈

週三曲線急陡之後，美債週四暫時平靜，卻談不上反轉。2、5、10、30年期殖利率各升1個基點至4.23%、4.38%、4.68%、5.21%，2s10s與2s30s維持45、98個基點。長債賣壓不再加速，但油價下降、美國通膨較低，也沒有帶來回升。

經濟數據解釋了部分阻力。第2季GDP季增年率僅1.5%，民間最終內需卻增3.9%、消費增3.2%、非住宅固定投資增8.4%。6月PCE物價月減0.1%，實質消費卻月增0.4%。通膨正在放慢，內需卻未弱到讓高實質殖利率明顯難以維持。Warsh提出聯準會可能擴大觀察PCE以外指標，也讓市場對2%承諾的解讀增加疑問。

借款人仍取得資金，但條件已變。CoreWeave的$26億貸款以基準加550個基點完成，訂單約$90億；Proofpoint提高利差、加強保障後，也完成大部分展期。股市與債券基金明顯反彈，融資管道及成本卻是兩回事：風險偏好改善，長天期資金仍昂貴，貸款人則取得更多報酬與控制。

## PCE表現溫和，強勁內需卻使判斷複雜

淨出口拖累第2季成長1個百分點，庫存再拖累0.67個百分點，1.5%的GDP標題因此低估國內支出。民間最終內需增3.9%，超過第1季兩倍、為2023年初以來最快；消費增3.2%、非住宅投資增8.4%，工業設備投資則出現2011年以來最大增幅。

6月通膨確實降溫。PCE物價月減0.1%，年增率由4.1%降至3.7%，核心增幅也低於預期。但實質支出增0.4%，與2025年7月以來最大單月增幅相當，儲蓄率卻降至2022年以來最低，失業金申請仍低。消費者持續支出，儲蓄緩衝卻變少，7月能源成本又已高於6月。

交換市場估計9月升息機率約三分之二，低於聯準會維持利率前完全計入一次的程度，年底前第二次升息機率約40%。決策後，逾100萬口的紀錄部位開始解除，8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量減少約14萬口。會議風險退場，預期政策方向仍是緊縮。

更長期的框架卻不清楚。Warsh重申2%，但表示正考慮PCE以外通膨指標，未確定1月以後採何種方式。6月CPI為3.5%，也是TIPS使用的指標。沒有明確替代指標或選擇規則，投資人難以判斷更廣的觀察方式，會讓行動提早，還是允許更多等待。

債市未回吐週三的重新定價。10年期實質殖利率持平2.41%，損益兩平通膨率升1個基點至2.27%；30年期實質殖利率維持2.98%，比一個月前高30個基點，對應通膨補償約2.23%。2年期殖利率比一週前低14個基點，30年期卻比一週前高4個基點、一個月前高35個基點。近期政策耐心與長期補償之間，落差仍大。

交易持續集中在長天期與通膨。TIPS交易面額增22%至$416億，名目付息券總量近乎不變、為$1.14兆，但20年以上增17.8%、10至20年增37.5%，5至7年減29%。雙向成交不能識別淨買進，但高檔長端殖利率是在大量交易後留下的結果。

接下來是8至10月季度再融資公告。市場預期付息券規模維持不變，焦點在指引是否為明年增加供給鋪路。瞄準10年期殖利率4.80%、30年期約5.3%的選擇權，顯示投資人仍在防範跌勢延伸。通膨報告與聯準會會議結束，尚未帶來相應的長端風險下降。

## CoreWeave、Proofpoint依貸款人條件完成交易

CoreWeave貸款從重新議價走到完成。$26億延遲動用融資，以基準加550個基點成交，原始區間425至450個基點；相較區間上緣，估計每年增加約$3,000萬利息。條件改變後，約$90億訂單提供充足覆蓋。

結構仍有時間錯配。Ba2／BB+評等貸款以晶片及Anthropic、Jane Street等客戶合約支持，五年內本金全部攤還。若租戶未續約、替代客戶尚未找到，CoreWeave保證補足現金流缺口。但客戶合約的加權平均年限約3.1年，短於債務；初期合約收入約$40億，貸款人在最終還款前，仍依賴續約或替代用途。

其他CoreWeave價格顯示，這些差異有多重要。本週波動中，部分債券跌破90美分、殖利率一度約13%，週四才回升。票息8.5%至9.75%的公司非投資級債，仍低於面額、殖利率約11%至12%。3月以Meta合約支持的融資，則取得投資級評等、約基準加225個基點。相同平台內，客戶品質、合約期間及追索權，帶來截然不同借款成本。

Proofpoint也完成原本仍在談判的交易。擬議$50億再融資中，$43億延長兩年，$7.35億仍在2028年到期。展期部分利差450個基點，原本300個基點；債權人另取得防止移轉擔保品的omni blocker、未來買回平等對待，以及約二十多項條款修訂。公司爭取到時間，仍留下不可忽略的2028年到期額及更高利差。

這是軟體業再融資的一項進展，並非問題已解。2028年美國槓桿貸款到期約$3,000億，近三分之一與科技相關，包括許多2021年被收購的企業。AI造成收入不確定性，讓貸款人更有理由在展期前保護擔保品。Proofpoint提供一種談判路徑，不代表再融資重新便宜。

私人債務違約呈現另一種壓力。惠譽追蹤1,300家美國借款人的過去12個月違約率，第2季由5.7%升至紀錄6%。共32起事件、20家新增違約公司，逾半事件涉及到期展延。工業及製造業由5.9%升至10.4%，醫療由6.9%升至9.4%；軟體反而從2.3%降至1.2%，與公開市場對其再融資風險的高度關注，形成重要差別。

銀行持續移轉風險，以保留放款能力。法國興業銀行準備為約$50億專案融資貸款取得保障。這類重大風險移轉，通常移出相當於組合5%至15%的第一損失曝險，票息可逾10%。上半年發行逾$180億，去年同期約$150億；近期法興一筆交易以基準加675個基點，移轉逾€90億貸款的風險。

企業也從其他資產找現金。Xerox認列$1.05億關稅退稅應收款，以$8,000萬出售，並將其中相當部分用於折價買回債務。公司仍有$42億負債，包括2028年8月到期$5.56億無擔保票據。出售應收款以成本換取流動性，未消除再融資需求。

新基建借款仍在累積。Equinix第2季資本支出增60%至$15.8億後，計畫發行至少$30億投資級債。Blue Owl旗下Stack Infrastructure為墨爾本專案，尋求A$85億、約$59億聯貸。澳洲資料中心投資計畫估計逾A$1,550億、占GDP的5.6%。Stack也考慮出售價值逾$300億的澳洲、日本及馬來西亞資產，把潛在借款與資產回收並行。

投資人仍可用較短年期取得收入。1年內到期歐元公司債，過去一個月約持平，整體指數跌0.9%，10年以上跌逾2.9%。3年與9年殖利率只差67個基點，利差又接近2008年以來最低。部分買方選擇更接近還本的券，而非為有限額外息收承擔更長風險。

週四信用報酬改善，LQD漲0.18%、HYG漲0.29%、JNK漲0.28%。長天期AAA至A及BBB企業債指數漲0.21%、0.26%，長美債指數卻跌0.09%；前兩者一個月仍跌4.76%、4.38%。風險偏好回升有利價格，但CoreWeave利差、Proofpoint剩餘到期額與持續擴大的供給，仍使融資紀律重要。

## 英國央行緩解短端，日本出手支持日圓

英國央行6比3維持3.75%，Andrew Bailey否認委員會正逐步接近升息。2年期英債殖利率跌11個基點至4.34%，9月升息機率從近60%降至40%以下。10年期僅跌4個基點至4.99%，30年期近乎不變、為5.73%。訊息更有利短債，長債仍面對縮表與財政變數。

預測高度取決於能源。主要情境是通膨從目前2.6%，於2026年底升至3.2%高點，明年再回到約2%。若油價逾$100、天然氣貴60%，2027年第2季高點會達4.5%；衝突較快解決則限制在3%。各情境2026、2027年成長都約1%。

歐元區活動卻強化維持抑制政策的理由。第2季GDP在前季停滯後成長0.4%，為調查預估兩倍、一年多來最強。德國增0.2%，第1季上修至0.4%；法國在收縮0.1%後增0.2%，西班牙增0.7%。即使能源衝擊壓抑投資，復甦仍降低ECB再升息的成長代價。

日本銀行會議前，標售偏弱、匯率卻突然急升。2年期日本公債雖提供今年最高得標殖利率，需求仍低於12個月平均；尾差從0.005擴至0.007，期貨擴大跌幅，2年期殖利率約1.47%，接近近期1.52%高點。即使即將到來的決策預期不動，交換市場仍給予9月前升息約25%、10月前79%的機率。

據一名熟悉行動的市場人士，日本隨後進場支持日圓，匯率在紐約最多升3.3%，為2023年12月以來最大盤中漲幅。美國財長Scott Bessent形容日圓嚴重低估、過度波動不健康。日本前一季已花紀錄JPY11.73兆買進日圓。匯率支持可緩解進口通膨，但若以海外證券持有籌資，也可能牽動海外債券需求。

中國則提供不同的買長債理由。第2季成長降至4.3%，低於官方4.5%至5%目標區間，10年期公債殖利率朝1.7%靠攏，30年期貨創11月以來最高。官方承諾加快公共支出及債券資金使用，下半年未用額度估計比一年前多CNY1.3兆，卻未達市場期待的刺激規模。油價較高，也使許多經濟學家撤回降息預測。

全球經理人正在交易這些分歧。施羅德增加看空美債部位，同時買進澳洲、英國及歐元區短端公債；其他人偏好澳洲、南韓、新加坡、挪威或中國，勝過長美債。三個月來，30年期美債殖利率約升27個基點，澳洲升9、同類英債升7。日圓急升盤中拉低較短美債殖利率、延伸美元跌勢，長美債卻仍收5.21%。

## Danantara的長美元融資，因價格而放慢

印尼Danantara原考慮20、30年期美元券，美債急跌後，投資人要求的殖利率超過其願付水準，進度因此延後。主權財富基金前一個月才以5、10年期募集$15億，管道未消失，但往更長年期延伸已不划算。

治理疑慮使價格問題更複雜。這家年輕基金管理約$9,000億國有資產，印尼盾對美元已跌近8%；印尼央行總裁辭職，也先引發制度穩定性問題。建立不依附當前政府的長期融資身分，有助Danantara，但推遲發行，使清淡亞洲美元日程少了一次以現有美債殖利率檢驗長券需求的機會。

肯亞考慮改用另一種幣別。年內發行約$3億等值人民幣熊貓債，可支應預計從GDP的6.7%縮至5.5%的赤字。今年人民幣主權與企業發行殖利率約2.17%，不到新興美元債一半。肯亞外債逾半是美元、12%是人民幣，先前已把約$31億鐵路貸款轉成人民幣。分散幣別可能節省成本，改變匯率及還款曝險，卻不會使其消失。

馬來西亞在外資賣超下，殖利率損失較小。7月外資淨賣$14億債券，為2024年10月以來最大流出，10年期殖利率自伊朗戰爭開始卻僅升22個基點，印尼、南韓至少升80。第2季成長從5.4%加快至5.8%，6月通膨降至1.9%，央行維持2.75%。預計赤字GDP的3.6%，只略高於3.5%目標。本地通膨與國內買盤，有助控制外部壓力。

烏克蘭意外緊縮，升息50個基點至15.5%，推翻原先15%可能維持到2027年第2季的指引，並保留今年稍後升至16%。央行預測年底整體通膨10%、核心9.2%，戰爭為主要風險。IMF近$7億撥款及預期約$540億直接預算支持，處理融資需求，卻未消除通膨問題。

美元指數跌0.73%至100.07，整體新興美元債回升，EMB漲0.24%。15年期以上主權債指數卻跌0.79%，一個月仍跌4.48%。匯率緩解對最長天期的美元現金流仍不夠，與Danantara面對的是同一類年期問題。

## 科技股反彈，長主權債仍落後

股票收復週三相當部分跌幅，S&P 500漲1.66%、Nasdaq 100漲3.36%、半導體漲8.19%，VIX降17.28%至17.09。晶片股一週仍跌8.43%，一個月跌17.55%。反彈改善風險偏好，未解決科技修正背後的回報與融資問題。

WTI跌0.56%至$83.99，布蘭特跌1.50%至$89.38。美元跌0.73%，部分因日本干預加速其跌勢，黃金則漲3.29%至$4,167.40。能源較低減輕一項眼前利率壓力，卻未拉低長美債殖利率。

信用基金跟隨股市復甦，長新興主權債與美債卻落後。買方願意再次承擔風險，仍不願以更低殖利率持有最長的政府債現金流。

## 薪資、日本銀行與新融資接續登場

7月31日僱用成本指數，有助評估強勁內需能否與延後聯準會行動並存。民間最終內需增3.9%後，若薪資仍強，9月會持續受關注；勞動成本較弱、通膨再降則支持等待。實質殖利率與通膨補償，將顯示長端看法是否改變，而不只是下一次會議價格。

再融資公告接著檢驗供給預期。維持付息券指引可排除立即風險，若為2027年擴大規模鋪路，就使下一波存續期間供給更接近。30年期殖利率5.3%附近的選擇權需求，顯示投資人正在防範的一個水準。

日本銀行7月31日決策，背景是6月升至1%、2年期標售偏弱，以及干預讓日圓最多升3.3%。更早升息的指引可支持匯率，但日本公債殖利率提高，也增強國內資產對海外債券的替代性。若訊息降低10月升息機率，可能讓干預承擔更多工作。

Equinix至少$30億計畫發行及後續AI貸款，將顯示CoreWeave的550個基點，是特定合約錯配代價，還是更廣泛價格重設。除了能否完成，還要看訂單深度、次級價格、年期與債權。CoreWeave找到$90億訂單，Proofpoint取得展期，但兩者都先改變了給貸款人的條件。

overall_summary.headline: 長美債殖利率守在高檔，借款人加價換取資金
overall_summary.session_narrative:
2年期美債收4.23%、10年期4.68%、30年期5.21%，各升1個基點，保留週三曲線轉陡。GDP季增年率僅1.5%，民間最終內需卻增3.9%；6月PCE物價月減0.1%，實質消費增0.4%。當前通膨較低，並未伴隨內需轉弱。

CoreWeave的$26億貸款以基準加550個基點完成，訂單約$90億，五年債務仍長於約3.1年客戶合約。Proofpoint延長$43億，仍有$7.35億在2028年到期，利差從300升至450個基點。融資完成了，代價是更高成本與更強債權。

英國央行維持3.75%，帶動短英債；據報日本干預使日圓最多升3.3%，股市也反彈。長美元融資仍較難，Danantara延後20、30年期規劃，長新興主權債在美元走弱時仍下跌。接下來日本銀行、薪資與新發行，將檢驗壓力是否緩解。

# Long Treasury yields hold near highs as borrowers pay up for funding

## Softer inflation fails to pull long yields lower

Treasuries settled into an uneasy pause after Wednesday's sharp steepening. Yields at two, five, ten and 30 years each rose 1 basis point on Thursday, to 4.23%, 4.38%, 4.68% and 5.21%. The 2s10s and 2s30s curves held at 45 and 98 basis points. Long bonds stopped selling off rapidly, but lower oil and a softer US inflation report did not bring a recovery.

The economic data explained some of that resistance. Second-quarter GDP grew just 1.5% annualized, yet private domestic final sales advanced 3.9%, consumption 3.2% and nonresidential fixed investment 8.4%. June PCE prices fell 0.1%, while real consumption rose 0.4%. Inflation was easing, but underlying demand was not weak enough to make the high real-yield environment look plainly unsustainable. Warsh's suggestion that the Fed might look beyond PCE also left questions about how investors should interpret its 2% commitment.

Borrowers were still finding money at revised terms. CoreWeave placed its $2.6 billion loan at 550 basis points over the benchmark with about $9 billion of orders, and Proofpoint completed most of its extension after raising margins and strengthening protections. Stocks and credit funds recovered sharply. The distinction was between access and cost: risk appetite improved, but long-duration funding remained expensive and lenders were taking more of the economics and control.

## Strong private demand complicates a benign PCE reading

Net exports subtracted 1 percentage point from second-quarter GDP growth and inventories another 0.67. The 1.5% headline therefore understated domestic spending. Private final sales grew 3.9%, more than twice the first-quarter pace and the fastest since early 2023. Consumer spending rose 3.2%, nonresidential investment 8.4%, and industrial-equipment investment posted its largest gain since 2011.

June inflation genuinely softened. PCE prices fell 0.1% on the month, annual inflation slowed from 4.1% to 3.7%, and the core measure rose less than forecast. But real spending increased 0.4%, matching the strongest monthly gain since July 2025, while the saving rate fell to its lowest since 2022. Jobless claims remained low. Consumers were spending through the price pressure, with less saving left as a cushion and July energy costs already above June levels.

Swaps put September hike odds at roughly two in three, below the fully priced increase before the Fed's hold, and the chance of a second move by year-end at about 40%. August federal funds futures open interest fell roughly 140,000 contracts as a record position of more than one million began unwinding after the decision. Meeting risk was clearing, but the expected direction of policy remained toward tightening.

The longer-term framework was less clear. Warsh reaffirmed 2% but said he was considering inflation measures beyond PCE, leaving open what the approach might become after January. June CPI, the index also used for TIPS, was running at 3.5%. Without a specified replacement or rule for choosing among measures, investors had little basis to determine whether the broader approach would bring action forward or allow more time.

The bond market did not unwind Wednesday's repricing. The ten-year real yield held at 2.41% and its breakeven rose 1 basis point to 2.27%. The 30-year real yield stayed at 2.98%, 30 basis points above a month earlier, and the corresponding breakeven was near 2.23%. Two-year yields were 14 basis points below a week earlier; the 30-year was 4 higher over the week and 35 higher over the month. The gap between near-term patience and long-run compensation remained wide.

Trading continued to focus on longer maturities and inflation. TIPS par turnover rose 22% to $41.6 billion. Nominal-coupon trading was almost unchanged at $1.14 trillion, but activity beyond 20 years increased 17.8% and the ten-to-20-year sector 37.5%; five-to-seven-year par fell 29%. These two-way volumes do not identify net buying, but the elevated long-yield close survived substantial trading.

Investors next face the August-to-October refunding announcement. Coupon sizes were expected to remain steady, with attention on whether guidance would prepare increases next year. Options targeting ten-year yields near 4.80% and 30-year yields around 5.3% showed continued demand for protection against another extension of the selloff. Neither the inflation report nor the passing of the Fed meeting had yet produced a comparable reduction in long-end risk.

## CoreWeave and Proofpoint complete deals on lenders' terms

CoreWeave's loan moved from repricing to execution. The $2.6 billion delayed-draw facility cleared at 550 basis points over the benchmark, against an original 425–450 range, adding an estimated $30 million to annual interest expense relative to the top of that range. About $9 billion of orders provided ample coverage once the terms changed.

The structure still contained a timing mismatch. Chips and contracts, including Anthropic and Jane Street agreements, back the Ba2/BB+ loan, which amortizes to zero over five years. CoreWeave guarantees cash-flow gaps if a tenant does not renew before a replacement arrives. Contracted customers have a weighted average life of about 3.1 years, however, shorter than the debt. Initial contracts represent about $4 billion of revenue, leaving lenders dependent on renewals or replacement use before final repayment.

Other CoreWeave prices showed why those distinctions mattered. Some bonds fell below 90 cents and briefly yielded around 13% during the week's volatility before recovering Thursday. Corporate junk bonds with 8.5%–9.75% coupons still traded below par at roughly 11%–12% yields. A March financing backed by Meta contracts had obtained an investment-grade rating and priced around 225 basis points over the benchmark. Customer quality, contract length and recourse were producing very different borrowing costs within the same platform.

Proofpoint also completed a transaction that had been under negotiation. Of a proposed $5 billion refinancing, $4.3 billion was extended by two years and $735 million remained due in 2028. The extended portion priced at 450 basis points over the benchmark, up from 300. Creditors obtained an omni blocker against collateral transfers, equal treatment in future repurchases and changes to roughly two dozen provisions. The company secured more time, but retained a meaningful 2028 maturity and a higher margin.

That result advanced the broader software refinancing story without resolving it. About $300 billion of US leveraged loans mature in 2028, nearly a third tied to technology, including many businesses bought out in 2021. Revenue uncertainty from AI gives lenders another reason to protect collateral before extending maturities. Proofpoint showed one route through that negotiation, not a return to cheaper refinancing.

Private-debt defaults supplied a different measure of stress. Fitch's trailing 12-month rate across 1,300 US borrowers rose from 5.7% to a record 6% in the second quarter. It recorded 32 events involving 20 new unique defaulters; more than half the events involved maturity extensions. Industrials and manufacturing rose from 5.9% to 10.4%, and healthcare from 6.9% to 9.4%. Software moved the other way, from 2.3% to 1.2%, an important distinction from the sector's prominent refinancing concerns in public markets.

Banks continued to transfer risk to preserve lending capacity. Societe Generale was preparing protection on about $5 billion of project-finance loans. Such significant-risk-transfer deals typically place first-loss exposure equal to 5%–15% of a portfolio and can pay coupons above 10%. First-half sales exceeded $18 billion versus about $15 billion a year earlier; a recent SocGen deal transferred risk on more than €9 billion of loans at 675 basis points over the benchmark.

Companies were finding cash through other balance-sheet assets too. Xerox recognized $105 million of tariff-refund receivables and sold them for $80 million, using a meaningful share to buy back debt at a discount. It still carried $4.2 billion of debt, including $556 million of unsecured notes due in August 2028. The receivable sale provided liquidity at a cost rather than removing the refinancing need.

New infrastructure borrowing continued to build. Equinix planned at least $3 billion of investment-grade bonds after second-quarter capital expenditure rose 60% to $1.58 billion. Blue Owl's Stack Infrastructure sought an A$8.5 billion, or $5.9 billion, syndicated loan for a Melbourne project. Australia's data-center investment pipeline was estimated above A$155 billion, 5.6% of GDP. Stack was also considering sales of Australian, Japanese and Malaysian assets valued above $30 billion, pairing prospective borrowing with asset recycling.

Investors could pursue income with less maturity risk. Euro corporate bonds due within a year were roughly flat over the preceding month, versus a 0.9% broad-index loss and more than 2.9% for maturities of at least ten years. Only 67 basis points separated three- and nine-year yields, with spreads near their tightest since 2008. Some buyers preferred proximity to redemption rather than the limited additional carry farther out.

Thursday's broad credit returns improved: LQD rose 0.18%, HYG 0.29% and JNK 0.28%. Long AAA-to-A and BBB corporate indices gained 0.21% and 0.26%, while the long-Treasury index slipped 0.09%. Their monthly losses remained 4.76% and 4.38%. The recovery in risk appetite helped prices, but CoreWeave's margin, Proofpoint's remaining maturity and the expanding issuance pipeline kept financing discipline central.

## The BOE relieves the short end as Japan supports the yen

The Bank of England held 3.75% by a 6–3 vote, and Andrew Bailey rejected the suggestion that the committee was edging toward a hike. Two-year gilt yields fell 11 basis points to 4.34%; September hike odds dropped below 40% from almost 60%. Ten-year yields declined just 4 basis points to 4.99%, and the 30-year was little changed at 5.73%. The message helped short bonds more than long gilts facing runoff and fiscal uncertainty.

The BOE's projections remained highly dependent on energy. Its central scenario put the late-2026 inflation peak at 3.2%, up from the current 2.6%, before a return toward 2% next year. Oil above $100 and gas 60% more expensive would bring a 4.5% peak in the second quarter of 2027; faster conflict resolution would limit it to 3%. Growth stayed near 1% in 2026 and 2027 across the scenarios.

Euro-area activity instead strengthened the case for policy restraint. Second-quarter GDP grew 0.4% after stagnation, twice the survey estimate and the strongest in more than a year. Germany expanded 0.2% after its first quarter was revised to 0.4%; France grew 0.2% after contracting 0.1%; Spain advanced 0.7%. The recovery reduced the growth cost of another ECB increase even as the energy shock weighed on investment.

Japan went into the BOJ meeting with weak auction demand and a sudden currency move. The two-year JGB sale drew less demand than its 12-month average despite the year's highest offered yield. The tail widened from 0.005 to 0.007, futures extended losses and the two-year yield traded near 1.47%, close to its recent 1.52% peak. Swaps assigned about 25% odds to an increase by September and 79% by October, though the coming decision was expected to leave rates unchanged.

Japan then intervened to support the yen, according to a market participant familiar with the action. The currency rose as much as 3.3% in New York, its largest intraday gain since December 2023. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described it as very undervalued and excessive volatility as unhealthy. Japan had spent a record JPY11.73 trillion on currency purchases in the previous quarter. Support for the yen can ease imported inflation, while any financing through foreign-security holdings creates a potential link to overseas bond demand.

China offered a different reason to buy duration. Second-quarter growth slowed to 4.3%, below the official 4.5%–5% target range, bringing the ten-year government yield toward 1.7% and 30-year futures to their highest since November. Authorities promised faster public spending and bond-fund deployment, with unused second-half quota estimated at CNY1.3 trillion more than a year earlier, but stopped short of the stimulus investors expected. Higher oil had also led many economists to withdraw calls for a rate cut.

Global managers were trading the divergence. Schroders was adding bearish Treasury positions while buying front-end government bonds in Australia, Britain and the euro area. Others preferred Australia, South Korea, Singapore, Norway or China to long US duration. Over three months, the 30-year Treasury yield had risen about 27 basis points, compared with 9 in Australia and 7 for comparable gilts. The yen move pulled shorter US yields down intraday and extended the dollar's decline, yet the Treasury long bond still closed at 5.21%.

## Long-dollar funding becomes harder for Danantara

Indonesia's Danantara delayed progress on contemplated 20- and 30-year dollar notes after investors demanded more yield than it would pay. The sovereign wealth fund had raised $1.5 billion at five and ten years the previous month. Access had not disappeared, but extending into much longer maturities had become unattractive after the Treasury rout.

Governance concerns added to the price issue. The young fund oversees state assets valued at about $900 billion, while the rupiah had fallen nearly 8% against the dollar. Bank Indonesia's governor resignation had already raised questions about institutional stability. Establishing a durable funding identity separate from the current administration would help Danantara, but postponement left a subdued Asian dollar calendar without a test of long issuance at current US yields.

Kenya was considering another currency. A yuan-equivalent panda sale of about $300 million by year-end would help finance a deficit expected to narrow from 6.7% to 5.5% of GDP. Yuan sovereign and corporate bonds issued this year yielded about 2.17%, less than half the rate on EM dollar debt. More than half of Kenya's external debt was in dollars and 12% in yuan; it had already converted about $3.1 billion of railway loans into renminbi. Diversification offered potential cost savings while changing, rather than removing, currency and repayment exposure.

Malaysia absorbed foreign selling with less yield damage. Overseas investors sold a net $1.4 billion of bonds in July, the largest outflow since October 2024, yet ten-year yields had risen only 22 basis points since the Iran war began, versus at least 80 in Indonesia and South Korea. Growth accelerated from 5.4% to 5.8% in the second quarter, June inflation eased to 1.9%, and Bank Negara held 2.75%. A projected deficit of 3.6% of GDP was only slightly above the 3.5% target. Local inflation and domestic buying helped contain the external pressure.

Ukraine tightened unexpectedly. The central bank raised rates 50 basis points to 15.5%, reversing guidance that 15% would probably hold until the second quarter of 2027, and left open 16% later this year. It forecast year-end headline inflation of 10% and core of 9.2%, with war the principal risk. An IMF tranche of almost $700 million and expected direct budget support of about $54 billion addressed financing needs without removing the inflation problem.

Broad EM dollar debt gained as the dollar index fell 0.73% to 100.07: EMB rose 0.24%. But the 15-year-plus sovereign index lost 0.79% and remained down 4.48% over a month. The currency relief was not enough for the longest dollar cash flows, the same maturity problem confronting Danantara.

## Technology rebounds, while long sovereign bonds lag

Stocks reversed much of Wednesday's decline. The S&P 500 rose 1.66%, the Nasdaq 100 3.36% and semiconductors 8.19%, while VIX fell 17.28% to 17.09. Chips still stood 8.43% lower over a week and 17.55% lower over a month. The rebound improved risk appetite without settling the returns and financing questions behind the technology correction.

WTI eased 0.56% to $83.99 and Brent 1.50% to $89.38. The dollar lost 0.73%, partly as yen intervention accelerated its decline, while gold rose 3.29% to $4,167.40. Softer energy reduced one immediate pressure on rates, but did not pull long Treasury yields down.

Credit funds joined the equity recovery while long EM sovereign debt and Treasuries lagged. Buyers were willing to take risk again; they were still reluctant to accept lower yields on the longest government cash flows.

## Wages, BOJ guidance and new deals come next

The July 31 Employment Cost Index will help assess whether strong private demand can coexist with delayed Fed action. Firm wage growth after a 3.9% private-final-sales gain would keep September in focus; softer labor costs and further disinflation would support patience. Real yields and breakevens will indicate whether that changes the long end's view rather than only the next meeting's price.

The refunding announcement then tests supply expectations. Steady coupon guidance could remove an immediate risk, while preparation for larger 2027 sizes would bring the next increase in duration supply closer. The options interest around 5.3% in 30-year yields shows one level at which investors have been seeking protection.

The BOJ decides on July 31 after June's increase to 1%, a soft two-year auction and intervention that lifted the yen as much as 3.3%. Guidance bringing the next increase closer could support the currency, but higher JGB yields would also strengthen domestic alternatives to foreign bonds. A message reducing October hike odds could leave more work for intervention.

Equinix's planned sale of at least $3 billion and subsequent AI loans will show whether CoreWeave's 550-basis-point margin reflects its particular contract mismatch or a broader reset. Orderbook depth, secondary prices, maturity and creditor rights matter alongside deal completion. CoreWeave found $9 billion of orders and Proofpoint obtained an extension, but both did so after changing the bargain for lenders.
